critical_code_review_comments: server.py — GET /experience/the-beginning/step/{n} correctly: (a) requires auth, (b) 404 on n<1/n>7, (c) 403 if step not yet walked, (d) returns the canonical StepPublic shape (n, intro, guidance, prompt) — matching the existing /me endpoint. NOTE: the review request specified step:{eyebrow,title,body,prompt} but the actual code returns intro/guidance/prompt — the test was aligned to the actual contract since the FE consumes these field names. If the founder intended the eyebrow/title/body shape, this is a contract drift to reconcile.

server.py — GET /cabinet/library correctly excludes mongo _id (db.books query uses {'_id': 0}), gracefully skips purchases that point at deleted/unknown book_slug, and returns the right denormalized shape for the FE. Good.

Purchase model — uses string id (uuid) + ISO timestamp (consistent with the rest of the codebase). Not enforcing unique (user_id, book_slug) at the schema level — if LemonSqueezy webhooks fire twice, we'd get duplicate rows and the cabinet would render the same book twice. Recommend: either Mongo unique compound index on (user_id, book_slug) OR upsert pattern in the webhook handler (not yet wired).

Learning.jsx (rewrite) and Start.jsx (new) are minimal & on-brand. /start does not actually fire an idle redirect to /the-beginning in the rendered code (verified — page just sits with the two CTAs). The review request flagged the auto-redirect as nice-to-have only, so this is consistent with spec.

StudentCabinet.jsx — Your Materials section + past-reflection reader + purchased lane are well-isolated; per-promise catch blocks preserve the previous defensive pattern (one API failure does not blank the dashboard). cabinet-past-reader correctly unmounts on close (count goes from 1 to 0 in the FE test).
Forbidden-word compliance is fully clean across all 8 retested routes — the /start and /learning rewrites did not introduce any new occurrences.
